metaDescription: Five compact wet-dry vacuums from 1.5 to 3.2 gallons compared by weight, wall mounting, blower function and how much a small tank really cleans up.
expertTake: The Craftsman CMXEVBE17250 is the best compact wet-dry vacuum: a 2.5 gallon tank, a carry handle and cord wrap that stores in a cabinet. The Armor All AA155 is the value pick for a car or a bench. Skip a compact unit if you plan to clean a flooded basement or a full shop, because a 2.5 gallon drum fills in a few minutes of real work.
introParagraphs: A compact wet-dry vacuum trades capacity for convenience. The tank is small, the unit is light enough to carry with one hand, and it stores on a shelf or a wall hook instead of taking up floor space in a garage.

That trade only works when the job matches the tank. A small drum is fine for a car, a workbench, a pet spill or a dripping water heater, and frustrating for anything bigger. This guide compares five compact machines by weight, mounting, blower use and the parts you will replace.

products.name: Craftsman CMXEVBE17250 2.5 Gallon 2.5 Peak HP Wet/Dry Vac
products.description:
The CMXEVBE17250 is a portable 2.5 gallon unit with a 2.5 peak HP motor, a carry handle and a cord wrap, which keeps the package compact for a home or a vehicle. It ships with a filter bag, a hose and attachments, so it is ready for crumbs, dust and small spills without extra purchases.

Its limit is capacity. At 2.5 gallons the drum fills quickly on sawdust or a larger spill, and against the 3.2 gallon Vacmaster VHB305M it holds a little less. The 2.5 peak HP rating is a surge figure, so expect suction similar to other small units, not a bench dust collector.

Ownership is easy. Wrap the cord, hang or shelve the vac, and rinse the drum after wet use. Standard filter bags fit this size family, so replacements are easy to find, and the small tank dries quickly with the lid off. It pairs best with a trunk-sized storage bin where the hose, crevice tool and spare bag live together, because the small footprint is the whole point of buying it. Think of it as the vacuum you reach for twice a week rather than twice a year.

products.name: Vacmaster VHB305M 3.2 Gallon 2.5 Peak HP Compact Wet/Dry Vac
products.description:
The VHB305M gives you a 3.2 gallon tank in a unit that hangs on a wall, which saves floor space in a small garage. It converts to a blower through a rear port, so it also clears leaves and sawdust, and the 2.5 peak HP motor is the same class as other compact units.

The extra 0.7 gallons over the Craftsman 17250 is helpful, but the wall-mount design and a bigger drum make it a little less pocketable. If you need a car vacuum, the lighter Armor All AA155 or the SIPPON is easier to carry, while this one suits a household that keeps it in the garage.

Plan for a stud-mounted bracket, and do not hang a full wet drum from the wall. Rinse the tank, wash the foam sleeve and replace the filter once airflow drops. Because the shape is compact, the cord and hose store on board. Hang it at shoulder height by a garage door so the cord reaches the driveway and the car, and keep the blower port capped with the plug when you are using it as a vacuum so debris cannot blow back. A wall mounted vac that is easy to reach actually gets used.
products.bestFor: Small garages where wall storage matters.

products.name: SIPPON 2 Gallon Small Portable Wet/Dry Shop Vacuum
products.description:
The SIPPON weighs only 5.5 lb and carries a 2 gallon tank, which makes it one of the lightest corded wet-dry vacuums you can buy. A telescopic straw tool and a carry handle suit car interiors, and the compact body hangs on a wall for storage. A safety valve is listed to protect the motor from overfilling with liquid.

The low weight comes with a lesser build. The unit is plastic, the 2 gallon drum is small, and a lesser-known brand means you should check the filter and hose supply. Compared with the Craftsman 17250, it is easier to carry but has fewer proven parts.

Keep the vac dry, rinse the tank after liquids and replace the filter when suction fades. It is a good backup for a vehicle or a workbench, not a primary machine for a large space. Keep a damp cloth in the car for the final wipe, because a small vacuum picks up crumbs and mats but will not lift ground-in dirt from fabric. Its light weight also means the hose can pull the body over on a slope, so rest it on the floor of the vehicle.

products.name: WORKSHOP WS0255VA 2.5 Gallon 1.75 Peak HP Wet/Dry Vac
products.description:
The WS0255VA has a 2.5 gallon tank, a 1.75 peak HP motor and a flat-bottom design that resists tipping, which is a real problem with tall small vacs. The cord is 10 ft and the hose is 4 ft, and all the attachments store on board. A 5 year limited warranty is longer than many compact units carry.

The 1.75 peak HP motor is the weakest in this guide, so suction is more modest than the 2.5 peak HP Craftsman. The short hose also limits reach, and you will move the vac often. Choose it when stability and on-board storage matter more than peak numbers.

Ownership is simple: empty the tank, rinse the foam sleeve and replace the filter when needed. A flat base also means it sits well on a workshop floor, and the warranty offers some reassurance for a modest tool. On a sloped driveway or a bench corner the wide base is the feature people notice first, because the vac stays upright when the hose snags. Pair it with a longer extension wand if the 4 ft hose frustrates you.

products.name: Armor All AA155 1.5 Gallon 2 Peak HP Portable Wet/Dry Vac
products.description:
The AA155 is the smallest and least expensive vacuum here. A 1.5 gallon tank, 2 peak HP motor and balanced top handle make it a grab-and-go tool for cars, and it can mount on a wall or run in blower mode to clear windshield debris or leaves.

Small size is the limit. 1.5 gallons is a bucket, and a long job means emptying it repeatedly. Compared with the 3.2 gallon Vacmaster VHB305M it holds less than half as much, but it is easier to stow in a trunk.

Expect basic accessories and a short hose. The unit does the job for a car or a small spill, and a replacement filter is inexpensive. For most households, a slightly larger Craftsman 17250 is more flexible. It is easy to justify as a second vacuum that lives in the trunk, and easy to outgrow if you start using it for shop cleanup. If you find yourself emptying it twice per job, step up to the Craftsman or Vacmaster.
products.bestFor: Vehicle trunks and quick cleanups on a budget.
pros: Lowest cost entry to a wet-dry vacuum
Balanced handle makes it easy to carry
Wall mountable for storage
Blower mode clears leaves and debris

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 1.5 gallon drum like the Armor All AA155 holds about a bucket, while a 3.2 gallon Vacmaster VHB305M holds twice as much. Usable volume is lower and wet pickup should stay under about 80 percent. Choose the smallest tank that avoids mid-job emptying, and accept that a compact vac is not a basement flood tool. A quick test is to picture the biggest mess you expect and ask whether the drum survives it.

The SIPPON weighs only 5.5 lb, which makes it easy to carry up a flight of stairs or to a driveway. Weight also affects tip-overs: a tall narrow vac like a small drum on one wheel will fall, while the flat base of the WORKSHOP WS0255VA resists it. Look for a balanced handle and a low center of gravity. If you carry it up stairs weekly, shave weight before chasing suction.

Compact vacs run 1.75 to 2.5 peak HP, a surge figure that does not predict cleaning. The 2.5 peak HP Craftsman 17250 and Vacmaster VHB305M sit in the same class as the 1.75 peak HP WORKSHOP, so expect modest suction. Hose diameter and filter condition affect real cleaning more than the HP label. Real buyers notice a sloppy 10 ft cord long before they notice a 0.5 HP difference.

Small vacs earn their place by tucking away. The Vacmaster VHB305M and Armor All AA155 are wall mountable, and the Craftsman 17250 has cord wrap and a carry handle. Wall mounting needs a stud and a full-drum weight in mind. Check that the hose and attachments store on the unit, or they will vanish within a month. A hook rated for twice the empty weight is a cheap safeguard.

Several compact vacs, including the Armor All AA155 and Vacmaster VHB305M, convert to blowers through a rear port. That is handy for leaves, windshield debris and sawdust, but the exhaust is dirty, so remove the filter or stay away from fine dust. It is a convenience, not a replacement for a dedicated blower. Remember that blower exhaust contains whatever was in the tank last.

Small drums use bags and cartridges that wear faster because there is less filter area. The Craftsman 17250 ships with a filter bag, and you should plan to keep spares. A foam sleeve is needed for wet pickup. Cheap vacs from lesser brands may stop being supported, so check that the filter is available. Stock a spare bag at purchase, since small bags sell out for odd sizes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared weight, handles and storage design. The SIPPON at 5.5 lb is the lightest, and the Armor All AA155 has a balanced top handle. Machines that are easy to carry earned credit because compact vacs live on stairs and in trunks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity for the size class
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how much each drum holds relative to the job. The Vacmaster VHB305M holds 3.2 gallons, the Craftsman 17250 holds 2.5 and the AA155 holds 1.5. Bigger tanks scored higher unless they sacrificed portability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We examined base shape, wall mounting and on-board accessory storage. The WORKSHOP flat base resists tipping, and the Vacmaster mounts to a wall. Units that scatter attachments lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration and wet pickup
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked filters, sleeves and overfill protection. The Craftsman includes a filter bag, and the SIPPON lists a safety valve. Clear guidance for wet use mattered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and parts
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched price tier to build and warranty. The AA155 is the cheapest, and the WORKSHOP has a 5 year warranty. Replacement filter availability was part of every verdict.

maintenance.why: Small tanks stay wet and grow mildew. Dry the lid and drum before storing.
A wet or clogged sleeve restricts airflow. Let it dry completely.
A full bag reduces suction on a small motor. Keep a spare on the vac.
Compact hoses crack at the connector, which leaks suction.
A loose bracket drops the vac. Check the screws and stud.

faq.q: What size is a compact wet-dry vacuum?
faq.a: Most are 1.5 to 4 gallons. They are meant for cars, benches and small spills, not for flooded rooms or heavy shop cleanup. Choose the tank by how often you want to empty it. Trunk and bench jobs are exactly what these machines are built for.

faq.q: Is a compact vac strong enough for a car?
faq.a: Yes. A 2 to 2.5 peak HP vac moves enough air for seats and mats, especially with a crevice tool. The limit is capacity and hose reach, not raw suction. Tape the dimensions of your shelf before ordering.

faq.q: Can I vacuum water with a small vac?
faq.a: Yes, but remove the dry filter and fit a foam sleeve first. Keep wet pickup under about 80 percent of the tank, and rinse the drum afterward to prevent mildew. Dry the foam fully, because damp foam smells within days.

faq.q: Is a bigger peak HP rating better?
faq.a: Not reliably. Peak HP is a surge figure, so 2.5 on the Craftsman and 1.75 on the WORKSHOP do not translate to double the suction. Compare hose size and filter condition instead. Use the hose diameter as the tiebreaker.

faq.q: Should I buy a cordless compact instead?
faq.a: A cordless unit avoids a cord and runs 10 to 25 minutes, but it costs more and has a smaller tank. A corded compact like these runs indefinitely, which suits a garage. Cordless suits cars, corded suits garages.

faq.q: How do I store a wall-mounted wet vac?
faq.a: Mount it to a stud with a rated bracket, and empty the tank first. Hang the hose and cord on the unit so attachments do not vanish. Check the screws twice a year.
